draft.title: A changing workforce
card: Australia's population is getting older. More workers are in older age groups, and many people work for longer before they retire.
More women are now in paid work than in the past. This has changed who is in the workforce and the kinds of jobs they do.
Workplace laws change over time. New laws can set rules about pay, safety and fair treatment at work.
Some businesses now take more social and environmental responsibility. For example, a business may cut its waste or support its local community.
draft.remember: The workforce changes as the population ages, more women work, laws change and businesses act more responsibly.

a.q: Which of these is a change in Australia's workforce?
opts: More women are in paid work than in the past
Fewer people live in older age groups
Workplace laws never change
Businesses ignore their social responsibility
a.why: The card says more women are in paid work now than in the past. The population is getting older, not younger, and laws and business behaviour do change.
a.clue: Pick the change the card describes.

b.q: A Brisbane furniture maker cuts its waste and uses recycled timber. It also gives some work to a local training program. Which change in the workforce does this show?
opts: Businesses taking on more social and green duties
The population getting older and working longer
More women working in paid jobs than before
New workplace laws about pay and safety
b.why: Cutting waste and supporting the community are ways a business takes social and environmental responsibility. Nothing in the case is about age, women's work or laws, so those are wrong.
b.clue: Look at what the business is doing for the environment and community.

a.best: More women are in paid work than in the past

b.best: Businesses taking on more social and green duties

problems.detail: Each distractor simply reverses a card line ('ignore their social responsibility', 'Fewer people live in older age groups', 'Workplace laws never change'). The right option is the only one that agrees with the card, so a student can pick it without understanding the idea. The distractor 'never change' also uses an absolute where the card says laws 'change over time'.
The clue 'Look at what the business is doing for the environment and community' points straight at the answer about social and green duties, so it gives the answer away.
The card says 'Some businesses now take more social and environmental responsibility', but the remember line says 'businesses act more responsibly', which suggests all businesses do.

proposal.title: A changing workforce

proposal.remember: The workforce changes as the population ages, more women work, laws change and some businesses take more responsibility.

a.q: Why are more of Australia's workers in older age groups than in the past?
opts: Many people work for longer before they retire
More women are now in paid work than before
New laws set rules about pay and safety at work
Some businesses now support their local community
a.why: An ageing population means many people keep working for longer before they retire, so more workers are older. More women working changes who is in the workforce, but it does not explain why workers are older.
a.clue: Think about when people stop working.

b.q: A Brisbane furniture maker cuts its waste and uses recycled timber. It also gives some work to a local training program. Which change in the workforce does this show?
opts: Businesses taking on more social and green duties
The population getting older and working longer
More women working in paid jobs than before
New workplace laws about pay and safety
b.why: Cutting waste and supporting the community are ways a business takes social and environmental responsibility. The business chose to do these things, and nothing in the case is about workers' ages, women's work or a new law.
b.clue: Ask whether the case is about the workers or the business's own choices.

a.best: Many people work for longer before they retire
